 ACLU questions presence of Milwaukee DA staff at Election Day polling places
 By 
 Isiah Holmes 
 - 
 November 17, 2026 5:25 pm 
 Voting rights activists and others gather at the Midtown Center in Milwaukee on the first day of early voting in 2022. (Photo by Isiah Holmes/Wisconsin Examiner)
 The American Civil Liberties Union of Wisconsin is raising questions about the deployment of investigators from the Milwaukee County District Attorney’s Office to polling sites during the 2026 midterm elections. In a Tuesday press release, the ACLU said that it had filed a records request to learn more, noting that the non-partisan organization Election Protection received numerous reports of armed individuals patrolling around and entering polling places in Milwaukee County on Nov. 3.  
 The ACLU has requested records involving the use of Milwaukee County DA resources including any plans, policies, training, staffing information, firearms permits, communications and complaints.  
 Tensions were high as the midterm elections approached after Trump administration officials did not rule out  deploying armed federal agents near polling locations. Those fears did not materialize, and Democrats across the country achieved historic victories on the state and national level.   
 But apparently the Milwaukee DA did deploy armed people to the polls. 
 “The program conducted by the District Attorney’s office appears to have needlessly caused significant confusion and apprehension among voters and poll workers, with, as we understand it, at least one Chief Inspector calling the police to report unidentified individuals with guns at their polling place,” said Ryan Cox, ACLU of Wisconsin’s legal director. “We have significant concerns about the propriety of this program — which would certainly be illegal if federal law enforcement engaged in similar conduct — and we need to know the facts.” 
 Jeffrey Altenburg, chief deputy district attorney at the Milwaukee DA’s office, pushed back against the ACLU’s criticism in an email statement to the Examiner. Altenburg said that the DA’s office “regularly engages in election integrity monitoring for major elections.” The program has been ongoing for over 20 years, Altenburg said, and involves sending selected attorneys and DA investigators who’ve received election-related training to polling sites “to ensure there is no interference with individuals’ voting rights.”  
 Alternburg said  the DA’s office notifies municipal clerks prior to visits, and communicates and trains with community groups, political parties and organizations like Election Protection in the lead-up to Election Day. 
 Altenburg added that the ACLU has been involved in these trainings as well. He rejects claims in the ACLU’s press release that DA staff were armed, stating that only DA office investigators are armed as they are considered active law enforcement. He said that DA staff checked in with the chief inspector at individual polling sites, and that their appearances were brief.  
 The Milwaukee Police Department did not respond to a request for comment. However, during an Election Day check-in on Nov. 3, MPD told the Examiner that DA staff accompanied officers to a call involving people handing out election materials too close to a polling place near a university. Those individuals were gone by the time officers and DA staff arrived. 
 “The intent of this program is to provide support to the community in making elections fair and accessible to individuals in the community,” said Altenburg. “Prior iterations of the program have routinely generated positive responses from the community.”
